newsitem.title: UK: Utd News says big interest in local papers.
newsitem.headline: Utd News says big interest in local papers.

text.p: Prospective buyers are showing a "lively appetite" for 47 local newspapers which United News & Media has put up for sale, United chief executive Clive Hollick told a press conference on Thursday.
"There is a lively appetite from rather more folk than we thought. We're not in a hurry to sell, we want to get a good price," he said.

United Provincial Newspapers, the group's regional newspaper division, has announced plans to dispose of 28 titles in south east England and 19 in south Wales. Analysts have put a price tag of around 50 million stg on the newspapers.
United plans to concentrate its regional newspaper activities on its northern heartlands.
Possible buyers for the title are thought to include Northcliffe Newspapers, Trinity International Holdings, Independent Newspapers and Newsquest Media Co.
The sale is part of United's restructuring after its merger with television and financial services group MAI which was completed in April.
Hollick said that a planned review of the group's businesses would be completed by the end of the year.
"This year's accounts will tell the full story," he said.

Hollick said that the exceptional items in the full year figures should not affect the final results by more than 10 million stg either way as one-off costs and gains should broadly cancel each other out.
United said it was beginning to make money from the websites it runs, saying that advertising on the sites was starting to produce significant returns in the United States.
The Business Services division, which includes trade publications and trade shows, generated 34 percent of operating profit in the first half.
Consumer Publishing was responsible for 28 percent, Financial Services 21 percent and Broadcasting and Entertainment 17 percent.
